note: Curated component notices matched against detected hardware names. Not a live recall feed.

components.title: 14th-gen Intel — BIOS / power limits matter
components.plainEnglish: High-end 14th-gen desktop CPUs were sensitive to aggressive motherboard power defaults. Prefer current BIOS/microcode and sensible power limits if you saw crashes or degradation concerns.

components.title: RTX 4090 — keep Game Ready / Studio drivers current
components.plainEnglish: Driver timeouts (nvlddmkm) are often software. Clean-install drivers if you get black screens; check Event Viewer GPU theme.

components.title: ASUS USB-BT500 vs onboard Bluetooth
components.plainEnglish: If the dongle fails to start, onboard Intel Bluetooth may already own the stack. Unplug the dongle or disable one radio.

components.title: Portable USB SSD — watch for retry errors
components.plainEnglish: External NVMe enclosures sometimes throw disk retries under heavy load or flaky cables. Prefer direct rear USB 3.x / TB ports and a short quality cable.

components.title: Intel I226-V ethernet
components.plainEnglish: Solid 2.5G NIC. Occasional link flaps can be cable, switch port, power-saving, or driver. Event theme: ethernet-link.

components.title: Crucial T700/T705 NVMe
components.plainEnglish: High-end internal SSDs. Keep firmware current via Crucial Storage Executive if you chase peak reliability.
